title: OSD can fail to show on lock screen
line: The volume and brightness OSD keeps showing on the lock screen however often you press the keys, instead of stopping until you unlock.
explanation: While the screen is locked, the greeter draws the OSD itself from plasmashell's osdProgress/osdText signals, but plasmashell also showed its own OSD window behind the lock screen. That hidden window kept rendering without being shown, and after a few show/hide cycles its render thread blocked in eglSwapBuffers while the main thread waited for it inside an xdg_surface.configure (gdb: QSGThreadedRenderLoop::polishAndSync on the Osd window), so plasmashell stopped answering D-Bus and no further OSD signals reached the lock screen until unlock. plasmashell now follows org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver ActiveChanged (and GetActive at start): while locked it hides its own OSD and only emits the signals, so the greeter's OSD keeps working.

commits.message:
shell/osd: don't show the OSD window while the screen is locked

The lock screen shows its own OSD from our signals, but ours was shown
too and kept rendering behind it, which could block plasmashell until
unlock. Now it's hidden while locked and only the signals are emitted.

BUG: 525165

media.caption: Master, locked: cycles of volume key, Esc, wait, volume key. The OSD stops at cycle 3 and never comes back; plasmashell hangs.
With the fix, same steps: the OSD shows on every press and follows the volume (85% up, 80% down).
Master: full screens of the same six cycles.
With the fix: full screens of seven cycles.

review.text: Clearly diagnoses why the lock screen OSD stops appearing after a few cycles: plasmashell kept showing and animating its own invisible OSD window behind the lock screen, eventually stalling its render thread in eglSwapBuffers and freezing plasmashell's D-Bus handling until unlock. Watching org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver ActiveChanged (and GetActive on startup) to hide and suppress the desktop OSD while locked while still emitting osdProgress/osdText for the greeter is clean and at the right layer, matching how Plasma Mobile already avoids redundant desktop OSD rendering. The async D-Bus handling and slot wiring are sound, and the before/after media cleanly verify the fix.
